exam_guide_revision: Not a certification. Practical Python 3.10-3.14 fluency track; official Python documentation and selected AnyIO/HTTPX docs reviewed 2026-09-19.

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; progressively harder typed code recall provides the scored signal.

authoring_notes: Python Fluency is practical coding retrieval, not beginner trivia or a certification. Questions use progressive recall depth: guided -> recall -> construct -> fluency. Short literals stay on one line where readable, unfamiliar data shapes and intent are explained, and most questions have one meaningful blank.

modules.title: Use Python 3.14 expression and functional additions

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ 3.14 added strict= to map(); with multiple iterables, strict=True raises ValueError if their lengths differ.

reveal.text: Python 3.14 added strict= to map(); with multiple iterables, strict=True raises ValueError if their lengths differ.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________(combine, left, right, strict=True) is useful when positional correspondence is required and silent truncation would be a bug.

reveal.text: map(combine, left, right, strict=True) is useful when positional correspondence is required and silent truncation would be a bug.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ remains lazy, so a mismatch is detected only as the mapped iterator is consumed.

reveal.text: map remains lazy, so a mismatch is detected only as the mapped iterator is consumed.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ 3.14 added functools.Placeholder so partial() can reserve non-leading positional argument positions for later calls.

reveal.text: Python 3.14 added functools.Placeholder so partial() can reserve non-leading positional argument positions for later calls.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________(str.replace, Placeholder, 'old', 'new') creates a callable that still expects the original string as its first positional input.

reveal.text: partial(str.replace, Placeholder, 'old', 'new') creates a callable that still expects the original string as its first positional input.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ Placeholder must be filled at call time, and Placeholder cannot be supplied as a keyword argument.

reveal.text: Every Placeholder must be filled at call time, and Placeholder cannot be supplied as a keyword argument.

modules.title: Use Python 3.14 parallelism and template strings

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ 3.14 t-strings use a t prefix like f-strings but evaluate to string.templatelib.Template objects that preserve static and interpolated parts for custom processing.

reveal.text: Python 3.14 t-strings use a t prefix like f-strings but evaluate to string.templatelib.Template objects that preserve static and interpolated parts for custom processing.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ = t'Hello {name}' creates a Template rather than immediately producing a str.

reveal.text: template = t'Hello {name}' creates a Template rather than immediately producing a str.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________-strings are not the older string.Template $-substitution API; they are a separate Python 3.14 language feature.

reveal.text: t-strings are not the older string.Template $-substitution API; they are a separate Python 3.14 language feature.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ 3.14 added concurrent.futures.InterpreterPoolExecutor; each worker has an isolated interpreter and its own GIL, enabling true multi-core execution with explicit isolation tradeoffs.

reveal.text: Python 3.14 added concurrent.futures.InterpreterPoolExecutor; each worker has an isolated interpreter and its own GIL, enabling true multi-core execution with explicit isolation tradeoffs.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ InterpreterPoolExecutor() as pool: results = list(pool.map(work, items)) uses the familiar Executor interface.

reveal.text: with InterpreterPoolExecutor() as pool: results = list(pool.map(work, items)) uses the familiar Executor interface.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ interpreters cannot freely share mutable runtime state; arguments/results cross interpreter boundaries through supported serialization mechanisms.

reveal.text: Worker interpreters cannot freely share mutable runtime state; arguments/results cross interpreter boundaries through supported serialization mechanisms.
